notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation focused squarely on guaranteed throughput and predictable unit costs. Customer runs real-time personalization + reranking for multi-tenant ad pipelines. Key ask: firm minimum tokens/sec for tail loads (peak ad auction windows) and hard concurrency caps per customer to prevent noisy neighbors. Wants a burst policy that allows 15 minutes of 2x baseline throughput but with pre-agreed token overage billing and automatic fallback to smaller model.

Details (raw CRM notes):
- Use-case: reranking + personalization in low-latency path; median latency target 80ms/token, p95 < 250ms for 1024 context.
- Traffic shape: regular baseline ~150k tokens/sec across pool, spikes to 450k tokens/sec for 6-12 minutes during peak auctions.
- Customer request: "We need a contract that guarantees X tokens/sec available to our reserved pool even during region-wide failures" (CTO quote).
- Proposed Redwood approach: reserved GPU pool (8x A100-equivalents) + autoscaling buffer + enforcement of concurrency caps per tenant + burst policy with two tiers (grace burst then metered).
- They insist on deterministic concurrency caps at the routing layer to enforce per-tenant TPS and avoid noisy neighbor impacts on latency SLOs.
- POC plan: 2-week dedicated pilot with synthetic replay of peak auction traces; run with pinned model variants (32-bit quant and 8-bit quant) to measure tradeoffs.

Operational asks:
- Audit log retention 13 months, integration with customer SIEM (Splunk), SSO via SAML2, KMS using AWS CloudHSM or customer-managed key.
- Data residency: EU tenancy for EU users; NA for US.

Risks called out:
- If Redwood enforces too-strict concurrency caps, perceived throughput can drop if routing policy misestimates TTLs. Need clear fallback: can route to cheaper compatible model under burst to preserve latency but at lower quality.
- Finance pushback: wants clearer cost per 1M tokens under reserved vs. burst.

Stitch notes: aim to get sign-off on min tokens/sec and burst billing model before legal reviews final SLA.
